13.1.crux: Every sound is made by something vibrating, that is, moving quickly to and fro.

cards.title: What is a vibration?

steps.text: Stretch a rubber band and pluck it
It moves rapidly to and fro: it vibrates
Touch it to stop the vibration: the sound stops

say: The rapid to and fro motion of an object is called vibration.
No vibration, no sound.
cards.remember: Sound is produced by vibrating objects.

cards.title: Musical instruments
say: Every instrument has a part that vibrates to make sound.

cards.title: Feel it

items.sub: Feel it buzz when you hum

say: Sometimes the vibration is too small to see, but you can feel it.

crux_points: Sound is produced by vibrating objects.
A vibration is a rapid to and fro motion.
Instruments have strings, membranes or air columns that vibrate.

quiz.q: Which part of a tabla vibrates to make sound?
quiz.why: Striking the membrane makes it vibrate.

quiz.q: When you stop a vibrating bell with your hand, the sound…

13.2.crux: We speak using the voice box (larynx), where two vocal cords vibrate as air from the lungs passes between them.

cards.title: The voice box

labels.name: Larynx (voice box)
labels.note: At the top of the windpipe

say: The lungs push air through the slit between the vocal cords.
The vocal cords vibrate and produce sound.
cards.remember: Voice = air from lungs + vibrating vocal cords.

cards.title: Changing your voice
say: Muscles attached to the vocal cords make them tight or loose.

cards.title: Different voices
say: Men's vocal cords are about 20 mm long; women's are about 5 mm shorter.
Children's are very short, which is why their voices are high.

crux_points: Humans produce sound in the larynx (voice box).
Air from the lungs makes the vocal cords vibrate.
Tighter, thinner, shorter cords give a higher voice.

quiz.q: What is marked '?' in the voice box?
quiz.why: The two folds across the voice box are the vocal cords.

quiz.q: Why do children have higher voices than men?
quiz.why: Shorter vocal cords vibrate faster, giving a higher pitch.

13.3.crux: Sound needs a medium (a solid, a liquid or a gas) to travel; it cannot travel through empty space (a vacuum).

cards.title: The bell jar experiment

steps.text: A ringing phone or bell is placed in a glass jar
Air is pumped out of the jar
The sound becomes fainter and fainter
With almost no air left, hardly any sound is heard

say: Sound needs something to travel through. This is called a medium.
Space with no air at all is called a vacuum.
cards.remember: Sound cannot travel through a vacuum.

cards.title: Three kinds of medium

items.name: Solids
items.eg: Ear on a table hears a tap; string telephone

say: Put your ear to a table and ask a friend to scratch the other end: you hear it clearly through the wood.

cards.title: Silence on the Moon

cols.head: On the Moon
cells: Astronauts can't hear each other directly; they use radios

say: There is no atmosphere on the Moon, so sound can't travel there.

crux_points: Sound needs a medium to travel.
It travels through solids, liquids and gases.
It cannot travel through a vacuum, which is why the Moon is silent.

quiz.q: Why can't astronauts on the Moon hear each other directly?
options: There is no air to carry sound
quiz.why: Sound needs a medium; the Moon has no air.
Liquids are a medium for sound; whales and dolphins use it.

13.4.crux: Sound makes our eardrum vibrate; the inner ear turns these vibrations into signals that travel to the brain.

cards.title: Inside the ear
say: The outer ear is shaped like a funnel to collect sound.

cards.title: How we hear

steps.text: The vibrations pass to the inner ear
Signals go to the brain, and we hear the sound

say: The eardrum is like a stretched rubber sheet that vibrates when sound hits it.
cards.remember: Sound → eardrum vibrates → inner ear → brain.

cards.title: Protect your ears

items.sub: A pin or stick can tear the eardrum

say: A damaged eardrum can lead to hearing loss.

crux_points: The outer ear collects sound like a funnel.
Sound makes the eardrum vibrate; vibrations go to the inner ear.
Signals travel to the brain; never put sharp objects in your ears.

quiz.why: The eardrum is the thin membrane at the end of the ear canal.

quiz.q: Why should you never put a pin in your ear?
quiz.why: The eardrum is thin and can be damaged easily.

13.5.crux: The size of a vibration (amplitude) decides how loud a sound is; how many vibrations happen each second (frequency, in hertz) decides its pitch.

cards.title: Oscillation and frequency
say: A to and fro motion like this is an oscillation (vibration).
The number of oscillations per second is the frequency, measured in hertz (Hz).
The time for one oscillation is the time period.

cards.title: Loud or soft, high or low
say: Bigger vibrations (larger amplitude) make louder sounds.
Faster vibrations (higher frequency) make higher-pitched, shriller sounds.

cards.title: Pitch around us
say: A lion's roar is loud but low-pitched; a bird's chirp is soft but high-pitched.
Loudness and pitch are different things.

cards.title: Measuring loudness
say: Loudness is measured in decibels (dB).
Sounds above 80 dB become painful to hear.

crux_points: Frequency = oscillations per second (Hz); it decides pitch.
Amplitude = size of the vibration; it decides loudness.
Loudness is measured in decibels; above 80 dB is painful.

options: High pitch: many waves close together
quiz.why: Waves packed close together mean high frequency, so high pitch.

quiz.q: A sound becomes louder when the…
A pendulum makes 5 complete swings in 1 second. Its frequency is…
quiz.why: Frequency is the number of oscillations each second: 5 per second = 5 Hz.

13.6.crux: Humans can hear sounds from about 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz; sounds outside this range are inaudible to us, though some animals can hear them.

cards.title: Our hearing range
say: Sounds below about 20 vibrations per second can't be heard by us.
Sounds above about 20,000 Hz can't be heard either.
cards.remember: We hear from 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz.

cards.title: Animals hear more
say: Some animals can hear sounds that are inaudible to us.

cards.title: Ultrasound helps doctors

steps.text: A machine sends very high-frequency sound into the body
The sound bounces back from organs
A picture of the inside of the body appears

say: Sounds above 20,000 Hz are called ultrasound.
Ultrasound is used to look inside the body safely.

crux_points: Humans hear sounds from about 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz.
Sounds outside this range are inaudible to us.
Some animals hear them; ultrasound is used in medicine.

quiz.q: Can a person hear a sound of 10 Hz?
quiz.why: Humans can't hear sounds below about 20 Hz.
These very high sounds are ultrasound; they are inaudible to humans.

13.7.crux: Pleasing sounds are music; unpleasant sounds are noise; even music becomes noise when it's too loud.

cards.title: Music or noise?
say: Whether a sound is music or noise depends on how pleasing it is to the ear.

cards.title: Too loud is noise

steps.text: Your favourite song at low volume: music
The same song blaring from a loudspeaker

say: Loudness can turn music into noise.

cards.title: Everyday sounds
say: Sort these into music and noise. Did you and your friend sort them the same way?

crux_points: Music is pleasing to the ear; noise is unpleasant.
Music played too loud becomes noise.
Different people may find different sounds pleasant.

quiz.q: A song played at very high volume is likely to be…
quiz.why: Even music becomes noise when it's too loud.

13.8.crux: Too much unwanted sound is noise pollution; it can cause sleeplessness, stress, high blood pressure and hearing loss, but we can reduce it.

cards.title: Sources of noise pollution
say: The presence of excessive or unwanted sound is called noise pollution.

cards.title: Harm to health
say: Very loud sounds can damage hearing permanently.

cards.title: How to reduce it

items.name: Silencers
items.eg: On vehicles, aircraft engines and machines

items.name: Lower volume
items.eg: TV and music at low volume

items.name: Plant trees
items.eg: Along roads and around buildings: they absorb sound

say: Trees act as natural sound barriers.
cards.remember: Silencers, fewer horns, low volume, more trees.

crux_points: Noise pollution is excessive unwanted sound.
It causes sleeplessness, stress, high blood pressure and hearing loss.
Silencers, fewer horns, lower volume and trees reduce it.

quiz.q: How do trees help against noise pollution?
quiz.why: Trees along roads and around buildings cut down noise.

quiz.q: Which is a health effect of noise pollution?
quiz.why: Constant noise causes stress and can raise blood pressure.
